highlights.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
highlights.summary: Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has gone to great lengths to hype the security of its new AI assistant Muse, claiming it is “built from the ground up for privacy and security.” A zero-day vulnerability that gives locally run apps and terminal commands complete control of the agent raises…
body: Meta introduced Muse a few weeks ago. The assistant “books appointments, fills out forms and handles customer service,” “proactively takes tasks off your plate,” and can “make purchases, generate images, create documents, and connect with your favorite apps and services.” The macOS app (curiously, there’s no Windows version) also works with a user’s WhatsApp, email, calendar, and social media accounts. When a task requires a tool that doesn’t exist, Muse creates one on the fly.

Of course, for Muse to do any of these things, users must first give it access to their accounts. This includes authenticating the assistant to each service and, because the app runs on macOS, giving it permissions to a broad range of operating system-restricted device resources like writing files to disk, accessing the mic and camera, and monitoring location and calendars. Apple has spent years developing these defenses to prevent installed apps or commands entered into the terminal from accessing these resources, clearly because the company considers them a security threat. Muse completely undoes these default measures.
points: Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has gone to great lengths to hype the security of its new AI assistant Muse, claiming it is “built from the ground up for privacy and security.
The macOS app (curiously, there’s no Windows version) also works with a user’s WhatsApp, email, calendar, and social media accounts.

highlights.title: Pokémon Scalper Reportedly Arrested After Punching Man in the Face Over 30th Anniversary Target Drop
highlights.summary: A Pokémon scalper has reportedly been arrested and trespassed after punching a man in a viral confrontation that resulted in a four-year-old child getting hurt in the chaos. A Target store in Lisbon, Connecticut is at the center of a viral incident that occurred on August 28, 2026.
body: The person who recorded the footage confronted the duo along with his girlfriend, who submitted the footage to PokéStreetz, an account dedicated to exposing bad behavior within the Pokémon TCG community.

In the footage, the four parties argued about the amount of merchandise the scalpers were making off with; the scalpers themselves proudly said, “Damn straight” that they were checking out with all that merch, rather than abiding by the two-per-person limit enacted by Target, and warned the couple not to touch their shopping cart.

The recorder and his girlfriend continued to follow the scalpers up to a self-checkout station, where one of the scalpers decked the recorder in the face, causing him to drop his phone on the ground. Scuffling can be heard in the background, along with a child crying.

PokéStreetz claimed that the recorder fell into this child, a four-year-old girl, after being punched by the scalper. The girl also reportedly fell in the impact and hurt her elbow; although the recorder “immediately” went to check up on the girl, the scalper fled, allegedly leaving his wallet behind.

highlights.summary: Major US networks later suspended White House TV coverage of Trump as he heads to New York for the UN summit.
body: CNN, Politico and MS NOW have said they will sue the Trump administration after the three US media outlets were barred from the White House.

President Donald Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the organisations of writing "fiction or lies" about his team. The companies said their reporters were denied access to the building on Saturday.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
Major US TV networks later announced they would suspend their White House pooled coverage of Trump, leaving a potential gap as he heads to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

highlights.title: Celia Birtwell ‘humanises’ Burberry in London fashion week closing show
highlights.summary: Textile designer brings florals, vines and smiley doodles to brand’s luxury checks for one-off paired collection. Burberry and Celia Birtwell are both national treasures of sorts.
body: Burberry’s designer, Daniel Lee, has always loved Birtwell’s prints. When the two met this spring, he fell for “her energy, and her zest for life”, and a one-off Burberry meets Birtwell collection that closed London fashion week was born.

Burberry’s calling card is a graphic check; Birtwell is all blowsy doodled florals and psychedelic snaking vines. “The check is so dominant and so brilliant that at first I thought: what can I do here?” Birtwell said before the show. She hand-painted a less regimented version, which Lee loved. “She made the check more human. If you are buying a luxury product it’s not a necessity, it’s an emotional purchase, so it needs to feel human.” A doodle of round, Smartie-bright faces from her archive, drawn 20 years ago but never produced, became another print of the season.

The mood of the show, held around the corner from Burberry HQ at Chelsea School of Art, was buoyant: charming prints, soft silhouettes, and the eclectic guest list that is as much a Burberry signature as the check itself: actor Fiona Shaw and footballer Djed Spence on the front row, with rapper Central Cee making a cameo on the catwalk.

highlights.title: Military milestone: Ukrainian naval drone sinks Russian kamikaze drone boat
highlights.summary: In the world’s first clash of the drone boats, a Ukrainian naval drone destroyed a Russian explosive drone boat using a remote-controlled machine gun turret. This comes as the war in Ukraine has already seen widespread deployment of such uncrewed surface vessels in combat, along with swarms of…
body: The lopsided battle took place on September 12 when members of Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence detected the Russian uncrewed surface vessel (USV) in the Black Sea and directed a Ukrainian Navy drone boat to intercept. The Russian vessel was “positively identified” as an Orcan surface drone with a “jet ski type steerable water jet” designed to ram targets and explode, according to naval analyst HI Sutton in Naval News.

Such Orcan drones have already been used to attack Ukrainian ports and ships. These often work in coordination with flying drones such as Russian Geran drones that provide aerial reconnaissance and can boost communication between drone operators and drone boats, Sutton explained.
In this case, the Russian drone was hunted down by a Ukrainian Sargan-3000 drone boat armed with a 12.7 mm machine gun mounted on a remote weapon station made by the Norwegian company Kongsberg.
“It was inevitable that there would be USV-on-USV combat,” Sutton told New Scientist. “We have seen the same in the air and on the ground.”

highlights.title: Spurs bottom of PL but more than £300m spent - where do they go from here?
highlights.summary: This time it was supposed to be different. After multiple false dawns for Tottenham Hotspur, the club had a manager with proven Premier League experience, and had handed him a £300m+ war chest - easily the biggest in its entire history.
body: Instead, Spurs find themselves bottom of the table after five games for the first time in 18 years, with their only goals a pair of consolation strikes on another dismal afternoon against Aston Villa at the weekend.

Things aren't quite as bad as the table suggests and had Tottenham taken any of a number of presentable first-half chances against Villa, they would have gone into the three-week international break silencing some of the noise around the club.
But instead, two points from five games and such a dismal record in front of goal has kept the spotlight firmly on them.

Though it is only five games, their struggles to find consistency have extended into a third consecutive season. Tottenham have now picked up just 18 points in 2026 and, since the start of 2024/25, still one fewer than a West Ham side who were relegated at the end of last season.

highlights.title: Got an Android Phone? Google Thinks You’ll Probably Want a Googlebook Laptop
highlights.summary: Apple lovers have long enjoyed seamless connectivity between their iPhones and Macs. Now, Google’s bringing that experience to Android.
body: iPhones and Macs are like two peas in a pod. Apple’s hardware synergy means you can launch iPhone apps right from the macOS desktop, respond to texts without picking up your iPhone, and even copy text on one platform and paste it on the other. That kind of seamless connectivity does not natively exist for Android phone owners at the operating system level.

Google’s trying to change that with Googlebooks, a new class of laptop. First teased in May, the company finally shared more details about the new OS at a media-only event in New York City last week. Like with Android, hardware manufacturers can make their own Googlebooks, provided they hit specific standards set by Google.

Today marks the launch of five new computers that comply with the Googlebooks standard, one each from HP, Dell, Lenovo, Acer, and Asus. These machines are powered by either Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip or Intel’s Core Ultra 3 (MediaTek also supports the Googlebook platform with its new Dimensity CX C10 Max chip, but none of the new laptops use the chip yet).

highlights.title: Is it true that … cycling affects fertility?
highlights.summary: Saddling up is only likely to be an issue for elite athletes – and those with low sperm counts. “Cycling isn’t big on the radar of fertility doctors,” says Prof Colin Duncan, a fertility expert at the University of Edinburgh.
body: For women, he says, the only time cycling is likely to affect fertility is when it’s done at extreme levels, such as the kind of training undertaken by elite athletes.
“Doing huge amounts of physical activity can lower body fat, and that can switch off the ovaries,” he says. “Elite athletes may stop having their periods and reduce their fertility.”

For men, things are a little different. Sitting on a bicycle saddle for prolonged periods can increase the temperature around the testicles, “almost incubating them”. This can affect sperm production, because sperm develop best at a cooler temperature – one reason the testicles are located outside the body.
But for most men, Duncan says, this isn’t something to worry about. “The testicles produce way more sperm than is actually required for fertility.
points: Saddling up is only likely to be an issue for elite athletes – and those with low sperm counts.
“Cycling isn’t big on the radar of fertility doctors,” says Prof Colin Duncan, a fertility expert at the University of Edinburgh.
For women, he says, the only time cycling is likely to affect fertility is when it’s done at extreme levels, such as the kind of training undertaken by elite athletes.
“Doing huge amounts of physical activity can lower body fat, and that can switch off the ovaries,” he says.

highlights.summary: Our 15-month investigation into death and surveillance along the US-Mexico border began with a simple question: Why did so many people die near government surveillance towers meant to help track and apprehend them?
body: This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

To answer that question, we looked through thousands of pages of government documents, visited the border multiple times, and interviewed more than 45 people, including current and former White House advisors, presidential appointees, Border Patrol agents, medical examiners, sheriffs, humanitarian volunteers, and employees of tech companies.

The result of our investigation is the first comprehensive map and analysis of deaths near border surveillance towers. Here’s how we built it, what decisions we made along the way, and what the data can and can’t tell us.

The investigation relied on knowing where migrants have died and where and when US Customs and Border Protection towers were installed. We analyzed cases dating back to 2015, allowing us to cover different border policies, presidential administrations, and tower technologies.

However, the lack of physical copies will make it a lot harder for things to leak ahead of its release. Given tons of footage managed to surface in August, though, it's not impossible for more things to make their way online.

highlights.title: 4 ways to address the failures we found along the US border’s “virtual wall”
highlights.summary: MIT Technology Review today published our investigation into how many people have died near the “virtual wall” of surveillance towers that the US government has installed along the US-Mexico border.
body: We found cases of people who walked undetected through areas surveilled by advanced, AI-enabled towers and later died nearby, where their bodies remained unnoticed for weeks or months. These cases reflect systemic flaws in the virtual wall: broken towers, algorithms that failed to detect people, and agents who simply did not respond to alerts.

This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

Each of these deaths should have raised alarms inside US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) about the flaws in the agency’s surveillance network. This is particularly true for cases near the latest towers built by the defense company Anduril, which continues to win major contracts and is poised to benefit from the windfall of federal money slated for border security. The US is set to spend $1 billion to triple the size of the virtual wall by 2034.
Here are four ideas for what CBP should do next to address these failures.

highlights.title: When is the point of no return in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's deadline for getting new characters on your side might loom ominously on the horizon, but the game is more flexible than it lets on. There are a few points of no return, but only one of them is irreversible: the one at the start of Act 3.
body: The first deadline you'll encounter is November 27. This is when each Flame Lord's first part ends, and you have until the moment you start the final quest that day to recruit other characters. However, it's not a firm deadline like in Three Houses. After you clear that act, you can go back and replay any chapter in it. Replaying is helpful for recruiting other characters, training them differently, or completing paralogues, and there's no limit on how many times you can replay a chapter.

There is a catch, though. For the changes you make in your Act 1 replay to show up in later acts, you have to complete the rest of that Act 1 again. It's a bit tedious. If your goal is recruiting a character you missed, and you're going to play a second (or third or fourth) route anyway, we don't recommend replaying a chapter just to recruit someone. Instead, pick them up on whoever's route you play next.

highlights.title: Get tested and talk to your partner: how to have safer sex after age 50
highlights.summary: At 51, I want many more years of a healthy, happy sex life. So I decided to compile my own guide. When I got divorced after 28 years of monogamy, I was excited to be having sex again, but had concerns.
body: Now, at 51, I’ve been wondering how important barrier protection is for me. Though I haven’t hit menopause, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) says that “by 45 getting pregnant naturally is unlikely”, and HIV/Aids prevention and treatment have improved significantly in the last three decades.
When I consulted with my physician, she said I should still “be careful” but didn’t provide specific guidelines.

Frustrated, I started researching. I found books on safer sex for older adults, such as Never Too Late: Your Guide to Safer Sex after 60 by Dr Shannon Dowler. But I wanted something more concise, like the pamphlets we saw as teens. I want many more years of a healthy, happy sex life. So I decided to compile my own guide, with expert advice about how to have safer sex as an older adult.
No sex is totally risk-free – at any age. This reality is reflected in the American Medical Association (AMA) using the term “safer sex” since the mid-90s, rather than “safe sex”.

highlights.title: The US spent billions on border surveillance. Why can’t it catch people before they die?
highlights.summary: When José Morales Bernal crossed the border into the United States on April 8, 2024, the day before his 32nd birthday, it should have triggered a chain of technological alerts and human responses.
body: As he walked through the desert in southern New Mexico that morning, he was within range of three surveillance towers. Newly installed by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP), they were built by the defense tech company Anduril and equipped with cameras and AI to automatically detect and track people. They transmit live video to nearby control rooms and can send alerts to the government-issued smartphones held by agents in the area, prompting the closest available to respond.

This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.

These AI-enabled towers are meant to give greater visibility across the 1,951-mile southern border, freeing up border agents from having to spend hours staring into video monitors. They were installed in this particular place to spot border crossers before they reached the nearby town of Sunland Park.

Infantino opted not to engage with the disgruntled members of the council, but in a letter sent to all 211 of Fifa’s member associations he has indicated his willingness to submit to external scrutiny for the first time.
In addition, Infantino also invited proposals to review Fifa’s internal decision-making processes, which he said would be discussed at the next Fifa council meeting in Zurich on 15 October.

“First, I will ask the council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of Fifa’s current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements,” Infantino wrote.

📚 Day 1 - Classroom: ignore Duo teacher and complete Spike's gameplay goals to earn rewards

🚨 Day 2 - Detention: playing Brawl during classes gets everyone into detention! Complete especially stupid tasks (like changing your in-game language) to escape detention and return to class. Keep an eye on our socials to know the tasks and respective rewards!
